name: Generative 'noodle' wind with no MIDI: one noise source into three parallel filters (slow-swept LP, high resonant BP whistle, mid SVF BP), slightly different free-running sine LFOs with light LFO cross-mod, and an LFO-modulated three-VCA mixer
goal: Patch a self-running wind ambience bed that moves without MIDI. Split one white-noise source into three filters: a low-pass swept by a very slow sine LFO (dark rumble that brightens and darkens); a band-pass set very high with resonance pulled well up but short of self-oscillation (resonant whistle); and a mellower state-variable band-pass in the middle. Give each filter its own very slow free-running sine LFO at slightly different rates, and let one LFO lightly modulate another. Mix through a three-channel mixer whose per-channel VCA inputs are driven by three more slow sine LFOs, centred so the layers drift in and out without ever disappearing. Finish with a bracket EQ to tame and a big wash reverb. For a generative noise layer under cinematic pads, this differs from our triple-bandpass pad, which filters a played saw, and from the recorded-whoosh skill.

source.title: DevOcean Modular - Create A Wind Noodle Patch From Scratch #modularsynth  #sounddesign  #synthesiser
source.transcript_note: Modular app walkthrough; route.py said COVERED but hand-check found no generative noise/wind bed skill. Factory patch names omitted.

prerequisites: Noise generator, three filters (LP, resonant BP, SVF BP), six free-running LFOs, a mixer with per-channel modulation/VCA inputs (Web Audio: AudioBufferSource noise → 3 BiquadFilterNodes → GainNodes driven by OscillatorNode LFOs, implementation note)

outputs.name: wind_bed
outputs.description: Continuously moving wind texture that needs no notes

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Rates, cutoffs and resonance are set by ear; the transcript names no numbers. Keep all LFOs very slow and slightly different.
Keep BP resonance high but not at self-oscillation: you want a whistle, not a tone.
Mixer modulation should be centred so layers move in and out but never go fully silent.
Sine, triangle and smooth-random LFOs give flowing wind; saws and squares make it rhythmic.

steps.action: Start a patch with output, a gain mixer and an EQ (disconnected). Add a white-noise oscillator at low volume, with a little extra gain on the noise module.
Channel 1: noise → low-pass, fairly closed. Add a very slow free-running sine LFO (no MIDI, no retrigger) to its cutoff, slowed further if needed.
steps.expect: Dark rippling wind that slowly brightens and darkens

steps.action: Channel 2: same noise → band-pass (RBJ-type) set very high, resonance pulled way up but not to a tone, to make a resonating whistle. Add its own slow LFO.
Channel 3: same noise → state-variable band-pass in the middle range, a mellower flavour, with its own slow LFO.
Make all three LFO rates slightly different, still very slow, and let one LFO modulate another 'just a touch'.

Mix the three channels in a 3-input mixer with per-channel modulation inputs (each channel = a VCA), in attenuation mode, bipolar depth set in the correct direction. Drive each modulation input with its own slow sine LFO at a different speed, positioned in the middle so channels go in and out but don't disappear.
Add a bracket (low/high-cut) EQ to tame the bed, then a big wash reverb. Save it as a patch, then explore by changing LFO rates and shapes on both filters and mixers.

verification: Patch evolves for minutes with no MIDI input.
Soloing each channel reveals a distinct band (low rumble, high whistle, mid air).
No two filter sweeps peak at the same time over a long listen.
No channel ever drops to full silence in the mix.
